method: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass. findings: The current public grid and adopted Appendix I CSAI pp.2–8 establish one September-2026 entrant pathway: ten six-credit units per earlier year and thirty open exchange credits plus eighteen taught credits and a twelve-credit thesis in the final year. The appendix explicitly carries the second and third years through 2027–2028 and 2028–2029. Hybrid Intelligence is the new subject, not old Knowledge Representation. Zero-credit GROW and optional electives are not extra scheduled credits.

First-listed exchange remains the neutral route choice. EER 3.7 permits approved partner-university academic study with non-overlap/coherence and admission conditions. The destination and courses remain genuinely open. No internship, compulsory lab or named minor is imposed. Earlier years complete programming and Statistics I before Machine Learning; programming before Advanced Programming; critical thinking/statistics and ten participant-pool hours before Research Workshop. Calculus, algebra, Python and ML prepare Deep Learning. All propaedeutic subjects and sixty postpropaedeutic credits plus semester-six entry govern the thesis.

Research Workshop includes an entire experimental or ML research cycle and report. The thesis includes supervised empirical quantitative CSAI research, code/analysis and academic reporting. Neither a meta-analysis course nor generic skills are treated as these separate requirements. The old thesis manual remains only a search lead. Dated current catalogue content and the adopted current programme requirements govern the finding.

The closest response materially joins AI computations and learning with human brain, cognition and language, rather than offering only broad psychology or general coherence. Re-read the roles of decision under uncertainty, search/optimisation, neural learning, robotics, higher cognitive functions, psycholinguistics and behavioural methods. Computational systems replaces advanced cognition with specific software/data/network/algorithm/numerical priorities. Cognitive/language replaces four systems courses with philosophical, interpretive and evidence-synthesis priorities. Distinctness is 37.5, 30 and 67.5 credits each way and qualitative priorities change.

All 51 interests and sixteen generators have explicit ownership. The responsible/explainable ethical-design direction has its own three generators and maximum-reached disposition, instead of being hidden in an omnibus cognitive/responsible candidate. BCI, emotion interpretation and human-robot interaction remain evidenced programme questions and directions, not claims that UCR supplies dedicated interface, emotion-engine or BCI training. Five course substitutions improve actual contribution. Removed clinical-health, lifespan and climate-persuasion material was considered within its real scope, not discarded because of unavailable enrichment.

Re-read every selected contribution against the current reference, including description-only evidence. Neurobiology is comparative and regulatory foundation; higher cognition supplies the stronger cognitive-neuroscience relationship. Psycholinguistics aligns to human language/cognition, not computational NLP. Behavioural modelling aligns to Statistics II, introductory methods to Statistics I. Search and reinforcement learning provide bounded AI1/AI2 relationships. Seventeen positive relationships and eight meaningful gaps neither force equivalence nor duplicate courses/components. HCI, simulation, hybrid pipelines, NLP, critical-scientific thinking and separate research remain explicit gaps.

All three schedules use actual covered Fall-2026-start offerings, exactly twenty-four unique courses/four per term/180 credits, first-year PPD and six or more advanced courses. Earlier formal prerequisites pass. Programming before vision, data before ML, ML before deep learning and brain foundations before cognitive courses improve advisory progression without new hard constraints. Psycholinguistics occupies its only planned Spring-2027 slot. Linear Systems was not forced into thirteen spring-only computational selections; no offerings are restored or inferred.

Read all three final labels and concepts, twenty-five external component titles, thirty-three selected UCR course names and descriptions, five notes, source URLs, block headings, partial/gap reasons and audience references through the existing field-to-renderer mapping. Exact unchanged shared description findings are reused. Authorised audience prose explains the material gaps; internal provenance remains internal. Optional independent research is outside scheduled credits. No workbook, enrichment, app or renderer changes, Shiny/browser activity, screenshots, modals, independent human review or release approval are claimed.
